summary.text: Doug Mastriano is a Republican member of the Pennsylvania State Senate for the 33rd District, which includes all of Adams and Franklin Counties, and was elected in 2019.
A retired U.S. Army colonel with a PhD in history, he chairs the Veterans Affairs and Emergency Preparedness Committee.

paragraphs.text: Mastriano's official biography describes him as a combat veteran and the son of a career U.S. Navy serviceman who was commissioned as an Army officer in 1986.
He began his career with the 2nd Armored Cavalry Regiment in West Germany and deployed to the Middle East for Operation Desert Storm in 1991.

During a thirty-year military career he served in Washington, D.C., the Pentagon, the 3rd Infantry Division and U.S. Army Europe, and held NATO assignments including a deployment as Director of NATO's Joint Intelligence Center in Afghanistan.
He completed his career as a professor of strategic studies at the U.S. Army War College in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, and retired from active duty in 2017 as a colonel.
He holds a PhD in history and four master's degrees, in strategic studies, strategic intelligence, military operational art and science, and airpower theory.
He is the author of the books Alvin York: A New Biography of the Hero of the Argonne and Thunder in the Argonne, and co-edited Pershing's Lieutenants.
The biography says he led the effort to locate the site in France's Argonne Forest where Sergeant Alvin York earned the Medal of Honor.
After being elected to the Senate in 2019, according to the biography, he has advanced legislation supporting veterans, first responders and public safety.
He is married to Rebecca Stewart, and they have a son, Josiah, who is a lieutenant in the Pennsylvania National Guard.
